newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian president sets elections for April 19.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian president sets elections for April 19.

text.p: Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov on Wednesday named an interim cabinet led by Sofia's respected mayor Stefan Sofianski and set April 19 as the date for general elections.
"Today I issued a decree dissolving parliament with effect from February 19 and setting elections for April 19," Stoyanov said at a swearing-in ceremony for the caretaker cabinet.
After 30 days of mass protests, the Socialists last week gave up efforts to form a new cabinet and agreed to elections 20 months before the end of their parliamentary term.

The caretaker cabinet, which will hold its first meeting on Thursday, contains several critics of the outgoing Socialist government, and abolishes the economic development portfolio created by the Socialists.
"It is very important that during these months we put aside our small conflicts and mobilise all our patience and decisiveness," Sofianski said after the ceremony.
Bulgaria's ambassador to Bonn, Stoyan Stalev, will be foreign minister, and the deputy finance minister from the outgoing government, Svetoslav Gavriiski, will take the finance portfolio.
Alexander Bozhkov, deputy leader of the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces and a former director of Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency, will be deputy prime minister and minister of industry.
The health ministry will be headed by Emil Takov, a senior doctor and one of the leaders of protests at Pirogov emergency hospital against the current Socialist health administration.

The rector of Sofia university, Ivan Lalov, is education minister, while the trade ministry will be headed by Daniela Bobeva, who resigned from the foreign investment agency last year saying changes to the investment law did not go far enough.

"I hope that the caretaker cabinet will win back confidence in the administration," Sofianski said. He said the customary ceremonial handover, where the incoming and outgoing administrations drink champagne together, would not take place.

Parliament met on Wednesday to discuss changes to the electoral law and a bill authorising the interim cabinet to negotiate vital loans. Deputies are expected to complete the eight-item agenda on Thursday.

Authorising the caretaker cabinet to negotiate with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) will pave the way for talks on new aid to accompany a strict fixed exchange rate regime to shore up the collapsing economy. After initial resistance, the majority Socialists agreed on Tuesday to support the move.

Police protested outside the presidency on Wednesday morning to demand higher wages after a similar protest by army officers on Monday and Tuesday won a promise that their pay would be brought into line with other state salaries.
State carrier Balkan Airlines cancelled international flights for 24 hours for safety reasons after technical staff threatened pay strikes.
On Tuesday, leaders of the five parties in parliament signed a declaration on principles for tackling the crisis.

They agreed the caretaker cabinet must speed up long-delayed structural reforms such as privatisation and closing loss-making state firms, cutting state spending, cracking down on corruption and the grey economy, and encouraging investment.

The IMF has said it is ready to send a mission to Sofia as soon as a new government is in place, and Stoyanov has asked for aid to stabilise the economy before introduction of a currency board regime.
